steps.content: The MBCC command room remains brightly lit deep in the night. The message that woke you from your sleep thirty minutes ago glares on the large screen on the wall.
JXU0RjYwJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU4MEZEJXU2NTM2JXU1MjMwJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU1NDE3JTBBJXU2NTUxJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU2NTUxJXU2MjExJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JTBBTEw=
The rapid tapping of keyboards by the network technicians weaves an impenetrable web, casting a heavy shadow over the hearts of everyone present.
You stand quietly to the side with your arms crossed, your fingers tapping rapidly in anxiety.
So, has the message been deciphered?
You finally can't help but ask.

steps.speaker: Technician A
steps.content: Please wait, almost done...
The technician's eyes remain glued to the screen in front of him, his hands never stopping. A few seconds later, the deciphered message is projected onto the large screen.
Can you... see... this... help... help me... L.L...
This is... a distress signal?!
Lore-Ley.
This name immediately springs to your mind—the instigator of the Elysiland incident who was found and taken away by the Underground.

Since returning empty-handed from Lore-Ley's residence, you've continued your search for her and the Underground. You devised many tracking plans and strategies, but the Underground is vigilant like always, leaving no breakthroughs.
Just when you were getting nowhere, you receive this distress signal from Lore-Ley.
Another technician's voice rings out at the same time.

steps.speaker: Technician B
steps.content: Chief! We've pinpointed the location of this message to an abandoned building on the outskirts of the city. The exact coordinates have been sent to your terminal.
OK.
You throw on your coat and quickly head out.
Special Task Force Unit One, come with me immediately!
The team's fragmented footsteps echo alongside the eerie dripping sounds and electrical buzz in the pitch-black ruins.
Tracing the source of the sounds, you come to and push open a tattered, half-closed door. When you shine your flashlight into the darkness, you can't help but gasp at the scene before your eyes...

Lore-Ley lies limp in a puddle of dark, dirty water on the floor, her head hanging weakly. Her tangled hair is plastered across her face, soaked to the point where you can no longer tell its color. Yet she still tightly clutches a cable pulled from the corner of the wall.
At the edge of the puddle, a severed wire hangs from the ceiling, still sparking with electricity from its broken end.
Perhaps noticing your footsteps, or perhaps sensing the light, she musters her last bit of strength to grab the corner of your coat.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: I feel... awful... Chie...
You sit at your desk with a furrowed brow, rereading Lore-Ley's detailed examination report. These few sheets of paper have weighed heavily on your mind like a boulder these past days.
When you found Lore-Ley in the abandoned building a few days ago, you immediately used your shackles to temporarily stabilize her condition, then rushed her to the MBCC for treatment.
Although her life is not in danger, the examination revealed that she is suffering from an extremely rare type of congenital hydrophilia...
This rare condition causes her muscles to weaken, and her skin cannot be exposed to air for long. She must stay immersed in water.
Now, with the aid of your shackles, she can leave the water temporarily to walk around, but must keep her skin humid. After consulting medical staff, you learn this condition cannot be totally cured.
However, these are not the only matters troubling you.
Accustomed to Lore-Ley's erratic and bold persona in the virtual world, you're surprised to find that she is completely different in real life.
Finally attaining freedom though, she somehow avoids meeting with people.

She almost never appears in the Recreation Area or Outdoor Activity Area, and always finds excuses to avoid group training and Sinner social events. If someone comes to sit with her in the cafeteria, she immediately picks up her tray and leaves, bewildering both the other Sinner and cafeteria staff.

During hypnosis and psychological therapy, Lore-Ley hinders her treatment by refusing to speak to the hypnotist and psychiatrist. Only when communicating via computer or comms does the situation slightly improve.
Continuing like this is not an option. For the sake of her treatment and future, you decide to talk to her face-to-face.
You ponder for a moment, then open the chat window on your comms device and send Lore-Ley a message.
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: How's your recovery? How are you feeling these days?
The moment you send out the message, your comms device pings with a reply.

<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Great! I can move around and try a lot of exciting things now! 
<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Thank you for saving me. 
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: You're welcome. 
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: By the way, are you free this afternoon? Can we have a talk face-to-face?
This time, she doesn't reply as quickly. Half a minute later, a short reply appears.
<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Sure.
When you enter the interrogation room, Lore-Ley has already been waiting for a while. Under the watch of two unfamiliar staff members, she keeps her head lowered in wary silence.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: ...Hello, hello! There you are!
Only after you tell the staff members to leave does she finally relax a bit. She lets out a big sigh of relief and greets you warmly.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Is there something important you needed to discuss with me face-to-face?
Since she asked so directly, you skip the pleasantries and cut to the chase:
I hope you can assist us in wrapping up the recent events.
A hint of confusion gleams in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Me...? Are you asking for my help?
Yes.
The Elysiland incident involves the Underground, but we have limited information. However, you've had direct contact with them.
I was just worried that experience might be a traumatic memory for you, so I wanted to wait until you feel better before asking for your help.
Upon hearing that she could be of help, she becomes thrilled, nodding vigorously at you.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Absolutely! Just let me know what you want.
After returning from Elysiland, I got your address and went to your place right away.
But unfortunately, you were taken away by the Underground before I could reach you.
What exactly did they want you to do, and why did they use dark web technology to help you hatch up the Elysiland?
Hearing the word "Underground," Lore-Ley purses her lips, her face ashen.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: What other reason could there be? They noticed my power and wanted me to spread Mania for them on the dark web.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: I didn't think too much at the time. I thought nothing mattered as long as I could create a utopian "Elysiland."

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: To them, the bigger the Mania explosion in Elysiland, the better. They want exactly what you don't want.
You squint your eyes, recalling how Lore-Ley almost wanted both you and her to go down with the island.
Lore-Ley nods, looking indifferent.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Yeah, I turned them down.
Why?
Lore-Ley mimics you and squints back at you with interest.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: What do you think?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: If it were the old me, I probably would have agreed, but now...
Lore-Ley picks up a small cup of water and pours it on herself.
The water drips from her clothes and forms a small puddle around her feet.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: I think now... I'm more interested in the real world.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: I also want to see with my own eyes what this so-called real world truly looks like. What is it that makes people willingly give up the happiness, excitement, and perfection of the virtual world to return here?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: ...But that doesn't mean I've given up on the online world.
Lore-Ley extends her hand to you. You smile and shake it, showing that you remember your past agreement.
So, is this the reason they "abandoned" you?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Yeah, that's right.
But your power should be very important to them, right?
Lore-Ley strokes her chin.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: They think I won't be interested in the real world for long. They say that based on my personality, I'll soon return to the dark web... to them.

options: Do you want to go back?

choices.text: Do you want to go back?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Right now, of course not. You haven't taken me to experience those happy things you mentioned yet.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: But after that... it's hard to say.
Lore-Ley lifts her chin up, flashing her signature smile.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: So, make sure to do your best!
It's about time to take you out for a trip, but...
Hearing your words, Lore-Ley sits up a bit awkwardly.
This morning, I heard someone say she wanted to chat with you, but you ran off after just a few words. She's worried she might have offended you somehow.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: It's not like that! I...
Lore-Ley tries to refute but can't find the words, her face flushing under your gaze. You don't badger her, and patiently wait for her to gather her thoughts.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: I haven't interacted with the real world for a long time. All my communication was done online, so I don't know how to do it.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Sometimes, even though I've thought about what to say, as soon as I look up and see the other person's eyes, my mind goes blank.
Lore-Ley gestures to you, trying to explain her self.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Mmm... it's a bit like what I saw online before, where if you don't write for a long time, you get "writer's block"?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Do you get what I mean?
Lore-Ley lowers her head, sighing in frustration.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: There are many interesting people in your Bureau. I'd really like to become friends with them in real life. But in my current state... it's hard to avoid misunderstandings...
This is the first time you see Lore-Ley so dejected.
No rush.
Integration and adaptation take time. Just start trying little by little, and I'll help you.

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Hmm...
She mutters a muffled response but continues to look down. You ponder for a moment.
You mentioned in your message that you can "move around and try a lot of exciting things now," right?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Yes, why?
Tomorrow's a day off. How about we hang out to see the real DisCity together? Wouldn't that be exciting?

steps.speaker: Lore-Ley
steps.content: Huh? That's what you mean little-by-little?
Well, I thought the Elysiland owner might prefer a more thrilling approach, don't you?
